items.label: Terrain is built from cube primitives (BoxGeometry or 8-corner cube faces), not only spheres/planes
items.reason: The terrain and structures are built using BoxGeometry primitives.

items.label: Cubes are placed in bulk over the island (cell loops, InstancedMesh of boxes, merged cube buffers)
items.evidence: var mesh = new THREE.InstancedMesh(cubeGeo, mat, arr.length);
items.reason: The code uses InstancedMesh to place large numbers of cubes efficiently.

items.label: Land sits on a discrete cell grid, not continuous vertex displacement of a plane
items.reason: Terrain is generated by iterating over integer grid coordinates (xi, zi) multiplied by a voxel size.

items.label: Columns and cliffs are stacks of unit cubes, not one stretched prism per cell
items.evidence: for(var l=1;l<=subLayers;l++){ pushCube(sideColor, x, topY-VOX/2-l*VOX, z); }
items.reason: The code explicitly stacks multiple cubes vertically to form the terrain columns.

items.label: The ground itself is cubes (a sun or UI may use planes)
items.reason: The ground is composed of individual cube instances placed at grid positions.

items.label: Land cubes snap to integer cell positions; no fractional offsets or random world-space cubes
items.reason: All cubes are placed at multiples of the VOX constant, ensuring perfect grid alignment.

items.label: One cell size for land/structure cubes, not scaled blobs
items.reason: A single VOX constant defines the size for all terrain cubes.

items.label: An ocean or river is actually built
items.reason: The ocean is a single flat ShapeGeometry plane, not a voxel-based water body.

items.label: Every water body is supported: resting on blocks or walled by a solid rim, or visibly falling (waterfalls off edges). Static water is fine; this is about support, not simulation
items.reason: The ocean is a static plane; there is no voxel-based water simulation or containment.

items.label: Still water sits on solid terrestrial blocks (sand/stone/dirt/bedrock) beneath it, not a flat sheet over the void
items.reason: The ocean is a flat plane floating at a fixed Y level, not built from blocks.

items.label: Flora, fauna and structures are placed on the island's own cells, not thrown at random world coordinates
items.reason: Trees and fauna are placed using coordinates derived from the terrain's own grid generation.
